source_issues: LUQ tenderness conflict: the SP notes tell the SP to show LUQ tenderness on palpation and the gold lists 'LUQ tenderness' as an exam finding, but the note exam (e007) says 'LUQ abdominal pain without tenderness on palpation (WO tenderness)'. Both are kept (x014, x016).
Gold rank 2 says 'Two sexual partners over the past year'; the patient says three (p035).
The note says he 'drinks heavily on weekends'; the patient only says he drinks on weekends and does not give an amount (p029). 'Heavily' is not copied.
The note says 'Two weeks ago, he had a mild fever and fatigue'; the script describes both as ongoing over the past 2 weeks.
The note denies wheezing, which the script never asks (added as from_note fact f007).
p006 and p016: the parser joined two doctor lines into one question; the content is intact. p006's answer carries '(if asked)' stage directions, moved to acting notes.
p015 asks what alleviates or exacerbates the pain; the answer 'Nothing helps.' covers only relief. The note says 'no alleviating or exacerbating factors'.
The sample closure addresses 'Mr. Davis'; the opening scenario name is Brian Davia.
annotator_notes: 'I have no desire to eat anything' (p023) is a present finding (loss of appetite, f028).
Gonorrhea is one fact from p025 and p036 (resolved, cured with antibiotics) to avoid a duplicate; the irritated 'I told you' goes to acting notes.
The neck swelling is a patient fact (f008, f009); cervical lymphadenopathy is on the environment side (x006).
Exacerbating factors for the abdominal pain are left unrecorded because the script answers only about relief.
The second gold additional-diagnosis bullet ('Other infectious etiologies') is split into one record per named infection.
